chapter_theme: Sivavakkiyar's cipher at its thickest: silence (மோனம்) in its many kinds, the whirl-point (சுழிமுனை) and the maiden (வாலை) in it, the syllables கூ and கீ, the red flame, the horn and the bow's curve, all naming what the breath finds when it climbs the five letters. Around this run the attacks: millions who call themselves yogis and jnanis, disputants, caste-talkers and dung-pickers, who search all their days and never see.
structure_note: 1289 to 1293 move from the five letters through the breath's ascent to an apophatic Lord; 1294 to 1298 and 1301 are the attacks, built on fourfold repetition (கோடிகோடி, வாதிவாதி, சாதிசாதி, ஆண்மைஆண்மை); 1299, 1300 and 1302 to 1313 are the cipher of the whirl-point, the maiden and the silences, nearly every one ending சிவாயமே or மோனமே. 1290 runs on into 1291 without a verb of its own.

1289.reading: Jnanis who recite the four Vedas and seek within the five letters where the running five senses are stilled: the three qualities in which the learned gather are within the letters, and Sivayam came to be as the dancing puppet.
1289.nuance: குணங்கள் மூன்று எழுத்துளே can be the three gunas inside the letters or the three letters (அ உ ம) of Om; the two readings are both open. ஆடுகின்ற பாவை, the dancing puppet, is the life or Shakti moving the body, as in 1286.

1290.reading: In the chakra of the worlds, in the space of the lord of the elements, the wind packed within the fire of the swelling lamp; at the gate where the two, sun and moon, move, changing the staff and climbing up, in the sporting space ...
1290.nuance: The stanza has no finite verb and seems to be the first half of a sentence that 1291 finishes. தவன and சோமன், sun and moon, are the right and left channels on the yogic reading tradition gives; தண்டு, the staff, is the spine; the space where the two play is the central channel. The wind packed in fire is the breath held at the root.

1291.reading: Mounting the vaasi gently in the silent five letters, after entering the sphere of light that filled up to the sky; in the measure in which he and I mingled in truth and experienced it, he is and I am not, and it became 'no one'.
1291.nuance: வாசி ஏறி, riding the breath, is the Siddhars' word for breath-practice, and the mantra is its mount. The last line moves in three steps: he exists, I do not, no one at all; the verse does not stop at the first. மவுன அஞ்செழுத்து, the silent five letters, is the mantra said without sound.

1292.reading: In the sword's sheath the sword is held; in the mouth's sheath the mouth is held; in the man's sheath the man is held, see what a rare art; in the foot's sheath the foot is held, and the nature of natures; in the day's sheath the day is held: you and I have seen it.
1292.nuance: Six times உறை (sheath, case) with அடக்கம் (held, contained): everything rests hidden in its own container, and the man in the body is one case among them. வித்தை, the art, is the trick of this containment. What exactly is contained in the day's sheath or the foot's is not said.

1293.reading: He does not praise, does not destroy, does not become a form of maya; he does not slip, does not rage, through all the time of time; he does not droop, does not stir, does not become pure incense; he does not ... and does not speak: the subtle of the subtle of the subtle.
1293.nuance: Twelve negations in a row describe the Lord by what he does not do, and end on சூட்சம் thrice, the word for the hidden subtle thing that runs through this chapter. சுவன்றிடான் is unknown to me and may be corrupt.

1294.reading: The bliss of the letter that was uttered as 'kū': millions say 'yogi, yogi' and never come to know and see it; the monkey mind swelling here and there like a palm, millions upon millions remain saying 'the One, the One'.
1294.nuance: ஆகிகூவென்று is obscure; கூ is one of Sivavakkiyar's cipher syllables (with கீ, ஊ, ஈ), which tradition takes as names for the breath or the mantra's parts. மனக்குரங்கு, the monkey mind, is the common image for restlessness. பூகம் (areca palm) is likely a tall, swaying thing; the line may be corrupt.

1295.reading: Millions upon millions of the world's people, seeking and seeking the First, their days passed in vain; searching and searching, their bodies wrinkled; joining and joining in crowds, millions upon millions stand.
1295.nuance: Four lines of fourfold repetition (கோடி, நாடி, தேடி, கூடி) act out the futility they describe. The fault is not the seeking but the standing in crowds (கூடி நிற்பர்) at the end of it: the search is social and outward.

1296.reading: He is not black, not white; the cause of the Supreme's standing: he does not sit, does not hide, does not become one or two; he is not single, does not die, does not cease, does not perish: the Beginning that one who reached 'kī' and 'kū' in thought has seen and known.
1296.nuance: A second apophatic list after 1293, which ends with a condition: the Beginning is known by whoever holds கீ and கூ in thought. The syllables are cipher; the plain claim is that the Lord has no colour, number or end.

1297.reading: 'Disputant, disputant': he does not know the silt; blowing and blowing, his light dimmed, he babbles; street after street he picks up bull dung; 'caste, caste, caste, caste': he does not see the letter SA.
1297.nuance: Each line is a fourfold word followed by a failure. வண்டல் (silt, sediment) may be what settles when the mind is still; ஊதி (blowing) may be the breath-practice done wrongly or the bellows of the alchemist; the bull dung is gathered for the sacrificial fire. சகாரம், the letter SA, is the first letter of சிவாய on tradition's reading, so the caste-talker misses the mantra's beginning.

1298.reading: Fools who talk 'prowess, prowess, prowess': the form of the First that is to be seen stands through all the time of time, having become a bond that is silence and song, having become shame, at the gate of the sea, here and there and everywhere.
1298.nuance: Almost every word is contested. ஆண்மை is prowess or manliness, and may be the boast of powers; வாதி may be a misprint for ஆதி (the First); நரலை is the sea, and its gate is unexplained, perhaps a body-place. The point that survives is that the boasters miss what is in front of them.

1299.reading: Returning from the letter 'ming' with 'kū', sleeping with the moon, the moon changes and stands; because in the whirl of the body's great point it becomes one, darkness ends, meditation is complete, and the flame-light is seen.
1299.nuance: அங்கமா முனைச்சுழி, the whirl at the body's great point, is the central channel's opening at the brow or crown as tradition reads it; the moon changing is the breath moving from one channel to the other. மிங்கு and கியானம் (for ஞானம்) look like dialect or copying errors. கங்குலற்று, darkness gone, is the one plain phrase.

1300.reading: The secret of the flame rising, the secret of the channel's end, the secret that rose dense and sat as one, the secret that is solid, the secret of the maiden in the wick, the secret the sea raises: the one who has seen and known these is the jnani.
1300.nuance: Six சூட்சம், each a stage of the inner fire; the jnani is defined as the one who has seen them, not the one who recites. திரியின் வாலை, the maiden in the wick, is the flame itself as Shakti; கழிமுனை, the channel's end, is the tip of the central channel on the coded reading.

1301.reading: Dogs who say 'jnani, jnani', millions upon millions; disputants who talk of a rainy day with no sky, millions upon millions; fools who do not see the nature of the selfless ocean say 'we knew it before' without ..., millions upon millions.
1301.nuance: வானிலாத மழைநாள், a rainy day without a sky, is an impossibility, so the disputants argue about nothing. தானிலா சாகரம், the ocean without self, is the state they cannot see. மூனிலாமல் is unknown to me; முன்னறிந்த may be the boast of prior knowledge or of knowing the First.

1302.reading: On the subtle horn, in the flame of the whirl-point, in the pungent flower at the gate where the Broad One dwells, on the shy horn in the temple where he lived, on the island of initiation Sivayam excelled.
1302.nuance: A chain of locatives in cipher. கொம்பு (horn) is the channel or spine; விபுலை, the Broad One, is a name of Shakti or earth; வீ is flower or death; தீட்சையான தீவு, the island of initiation, is the place the guru's initiation opens. The whole is a map of the body that I cannot read with confidence.

1303.reading: The silence that surged, the silence enclosed, the silence that stayed, the silence that wavered, the silence that is the Ganga, the silence that burst forth, the silence that is the moon: these are the silence in which Siva stood.
1303.nuance: Seven kinds of மோனம் and an eighth that is Siva's own. The verse makes silence a thing with states, like the breath, and Siva's silence the sum of them. The Ganga and the moon are both on Siva's head and both yogic figures for the flow at the crown.

1304.reading: In the street of silence, in the maiden of the whirl-point, in the street of drinking, in the red flame that clung, in the corner of knowledge, at the gate where the sea rests, the red flame of 'ōn' rose: Sivayam.
1304.nuance: ஓனம் is probably ஓம்; பானம் (drinking) may be the drinking of nectar or a misprint for பானு (sun). The locatives (street, corner, gate) are the body's ways. The one event is the rising of the red flame.

1305.reading: The maiden who rose, the maiden who wearied, the maiden who sprang up, the maiden who is morning, the maiden who rose esteemed, and the knowledge that stood hidden: boiling up and massing together, they became 'kū' and 'kī'.
1305.nuance: Five வாலை, the young goddess as the power in the body, in five states, resolve into the two cipher syllables. The structure matches 1303's silences; the maiden's states may be stages of the breath, which the morning (காலை) suggests.

1306.reading: 'Kū' and 'kī' becoming silence, the principle of principles; in the spreading of the triple flame that rose in 'mū'; the fullness that fits as honey fits in the flower; breath, breath, breath, breath: it reached the hearts of the loving.
1306.nuance: The honey in the flower is the one clear image: the fullness is in the body as sweetness is in the blossom, neither outside nor added. முச்சுடர், the three flames, are sun, moon and fire on the usual reading. ஆவி, breath or spirit, repeated four times, carries it to the அன்பர்.

1307.reading: Men who talk of prowess: see, as a thing to be seen, the street together with the sun; then you can cut away the dross; the pillar-like subtlety of the First becomes radiance; it is the nada that danced at the gate of shame.
1307.nuance: அருக்கனோடும் வீதி, the street with the sun, is the right channel or the sun-path of the breath on the coded reading. வாதி again for ஆதி. கசடறுக்க, cutting dross, is the metallurgist's word for refining. நாண்மை is unclear, perhaps the day (நாள்) or shame.

1308.reading: In the shade where nada danced at the gate, in the street of the Veda, in the triple flame spread wide, in the 'kī' that is song, in the 'kū' that stirred: I know the refuge, the gate of the elements, the Beginning.
1308.nuance: புகல் அறிவன், I know the refuge, is the only first-person claim in a run of locatives. பூதமான வாயில், the gate of the elements, is the body on the simplest reading; the Beginning is found there.

1309.reading: Breath, breath, breath, breath, the breath of the five horns; dwelling and dwelling on the earth, men; the idle do not know it, though it is here and here; sinners, sinners, men fallen on the ground.
1309.nuance: ஐந்து கொம்பின் ஆவி, the breath of the five horns, is the life moving in the five senses or elements. The fourfold words (ஆவி, மேவி, வாவி, பாவி) rhyme the breath with the men who never notice it. வாவி is a tank or a call; the line is unclear.

1310.reading: The light that sprouted in the seed, in the middle of the bow's curve, shining in the pearl, the lamp that is silence; they do not know the Lord who is like the mass within the conch; the subtlety of the maiden lying and rolling in the wick.
1310.nuance: வில்வளையின் மத்தி, the middle of the bow's curve, is the point between the eyebrows on the usual reading, the bows being the brows (compare 1324, 1325). நத்து is the conch or snail, and the Lord is the body within its shell. வத்து is read as வர்த்தி, the wick, after 1300.

1311.reading: The silence that drains and swells, evening with morning; men who know how evening becomes morning; the red flame sprouting in the angle of the corner; the silence that stayed, having left the lullaby and the sun.
1311.nuance: மாலையோடு காலை, evening and morning, may be the two breaths or the two channels, so that knowing how one turns into the other is knowing the breath's change. தாலை (lullaby) and பானு (sun) in the last line are obscure in context.

1312.reading: The nada that hurried in the street of silence: speed without flaw, what speed is that speed! In the corner of song, in the ripened maiden, the red flame of knowledge walked: Sivayam.
1312.nuance: The one verse of this run that admires rather than maps: வேகம் என்ன வேகமே is an exclamation at the speed of the inner sound. கானம் is song or forest; the maiden is ripe (கனிந்த), as a fruit, before the flame moves.

1313.reading: In the street of the crown's middle, in the kind that remained, the fresh moon spreading and sporting; the lamp that is vermilion, the silence that is meditation, the silence that is bound: Sivayam passed beyond.
1313.nuance: உச்சி மத்தி, the middle of the crown, is the highest centre. ஒழிந்திருந்த சாதி, the kind or caste that remained, is odd; it may mean what is left when all else is gone. செச்சி (vermilion, or the plant of that name) and கச்சி are rhyme words whose sense I cannot fix. கடந்ததே, passed beyond, closes the chapter.

links.note: Both put வாசி, the breath, inside the five letters: Tirumular's root ground is நமசிவாய and spoken becomes வாசிய, its yoga தயாவாசி; Sivavakkiyar rides the vaasi up the silent five letters into the sphere of light.

The restless mind is a monkey in both: Tirumular says those who mark a boundary can bag the monkey, Sivavakkiyar that the monkey mind of the self-styled yogis swells here and there while they repeat 'the One'.
The Njanak-kummi's mad monkey mind, possessed and dancing, is to be tamed with medicine before the horse can be driven; Sivavakkiyar's monkey mind leaps about in millions who call themselves yogis.
The Naladiyar says 'good caste' and 'bad caste' are words with nothing behind them; Sivavakkiyar's 'caste, caste, caste, caste' is such a word, and the one who says it never sees the letter SA.

Tirumular's false gurus have looked over mantra, yoga, jnana and release without reflecting or making anything clear; Sivavakkiyar's millions who cry 'jnani, jnani' and claim to have known it before are the same men.

The Thirumular-njanam makes the suzhumunai the pillar where the two lights rise and set and the light that is the true object; Sivavakkiyar places Sivayam in the flame of the whirl-point on the subtle horn.

Tirumular defines silence as speech and mind both still, and separates it from mere muteness; Sivavakkiyar takes silence so defined and multiplies it into seven kinds whose sum is the silence in which Siva stands.

source_issues: 1290 has no finite verb and reads as the first half of a sentence that 1291 completes; the division may be the editor's.
1294 line 1 ஆகிகூவென்று and line 3 பூகமாய் are obscure and may be corrupt.
1299 line 1 மிங்கு and line 4 கியானம் (for ஞானம்) look like dialect spellings or copying errors.
1298 line 2 and 1307 line 3 வாதி is probably ஆதி (the First), as the sense requires.
1293 line 4 சுவன்றிடான் and 1301 line 4 மூனிலாமல் are words I cannot identify.
